items.title: From coffee to commute, the Iran war is shaping our morning routines
items.description: This century's biggest oil shock is entering its sixth month, with no end in sight as war in Iran continues. Is it showing up in your daily budget?

items.title: How the Trump administration runs Venezuela and takes its money
items.description: Amid the fallout of devastating twin earthquakes Donald Trump says the US has been taking "billions and billions of dollars from Venezuela". So who is running the country and what is happening with the seized funds?

items.title: Chinese AI shakes up global markets
items.description: A new wave of cheaper, powerful Chinese AI models are gaining traction and challenging the dominance of US tech giants Anthropic and OpenAI.

items.title: Trump's Hamas plan a 'huge moment' that raises a lot of questions
items.description: Middle East analysts are sceptical Hamas will willingly lay down its weapons and that Israel will totally withdraw from Gaza.

items.title: Funeral held for 'bright spark' 13-year-old allegedly murdered by teen boy
items.description: Hundreds of mourners gather in Victoria's west to say farewell to 13-year-old Layla Jeffrey after her remains were found earlier this month.

items.title: NDIS provider pockets $1 million after incorrectly billing participants
items.description: Some NDIS service providers have been referred to the ACCC as the government reveals thousands have been engaging in questionable billing practices, including using funds to pay for float tanks and golf lessons.

items.title: Live: Aussie teen tastes walk race glory, Kennedy eyeing pole vault gold
items.description: Flag bearer Nina Kennedy goes for gold in the pole vault and Australia's sprint stars return to the track after a host of medals at the velodrome. Follow live.

items.title: Spain says Ceuta migrant surge largely reversed as most return to Morocco
items.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has blamed trafficking gangs as Spanish authorities say at least 19 people were found dead in the water.

items.title: Nirmal Purja among climbers missing in Pakistan as rescuers find four bodies
items.description: Adverse weather is hampering rescue efforts on Pakistan's Broad Peak to find the missing climbers who were being led by renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja.

items.title: Politics were the focus, but Bluey stole the show at Garma
items.description: The first day of the nation's biggest Indigenous gathering was political, but the must-see guest was not a member of parliament.

items.title: Infantino's advisor quits as FIFA's World Cup plan triggers backlash
items.description: A senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino resigned in protest at plans to sell a stake in the World Cup.

items.title: Gina Rinehart puts ABC on notice over Race Around the World episode
items.description: Hancock Prospecting has formally placed ABC Chair Kim Williams AM, Deputy Chair Lisa Caffery and Managing Director Hugh Marks on notice and foreshadowed possible legal action.

items.title: More than 40,000 migrants from Morocco pour into Spanish border territory
items.description: Spanish authorities estimate more than 40,000 Moroccan migrants have crossed into the autonomous city of Ceuta on Thursday, sending its military units to bolster reinforcement.

items.title: 'Somewhat racist': Does the Grammys need an 'Asian' category?
items.description: K-pop powerhouse BTS's decision to boycott the upcoming Grammys after the introduction of an 'Asian' pop prize has prompted questions about the need for a separate category.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Testing your knowledge of Get Smart, Snoopy and liking piña coladas
items.description: Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right, the other is wrong. But there's a catch.

items.title: Viral hit The Polygamist raises issues — and eyebrows
items.description: The Netflix show The Polygamist prompts strong reactions online, while opening up some important community discussions around fidelity and addiction.

items.title: Hobart deputy mayor snack matter referred to police
items.description: The Hobart city council has voted to refer a matter concerning its deputy lord mayor and the taking home of snacks to Tasmania Police and the director of local government.

items.title: Six Fijians found clinging to planks of wood after 36 hours lost at sea
items.description: Six Fiji health workers survive a harrowing ordeal at sea thanks to a former classmate of one of the survivors.

items.title: Sri Lanka sentences officials to death over bombing that killed Australians
items.description: The 2019 Easter Sunday bombings on churches and luxury tourist hotels killed more than 260 people, including two Australians.

items.title: From bedrotting to erotic art by Lucy Liu, these artists know about being lonely
items.description: So many people around the world are lonely. But how do you capture the feeling? A new exhibition brings together 11 artists, including Lucy Liu, to make you less lonely.

items.title: 'We're not going to the finals': Storm set for 16-year first after loss
items.description: Melbourne Storm coach Craig Bellamy has conceded his side will not be playing finals in 2026, with the club set to miss out for just the fourth time in its history.

items.title: Freo all but seal minor premiership with hard-fought win over Bulldogs
items.description: Fremantle is an effective certainty to win the minor premiership after a hard-fought 37-point win over the Western Bulldogs.

items.title: Escort agency bosses lied about model's disappearance, coroner finds
items.description: A NSW deputy state coroner has found evidence escort agency bosses knew what happened to Revelle Balmain, who vanished in 1994.

items.title: Why farmers are spreading crushed glass on their crops
items.description: Recycled glass is being turned into a silicon-rich soil additive that farmers say is improving crop growth while creating a new use for millions of discarded bottles.

items.title: Slow-motion big ship lift operation thrills spectators in Hobart
items.description: Peering through binoculars and nestled on camp chairs, onlookers encircle Hobart's River Derwent to behold one of the most complex marine undertakings in Tasmania's history.
